4860.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know 総理 beforehand as well.

examples.en: We overslept on the same day. It’s like we’re really in sync, isn’t it.
examples.ja: 同じ日に朝寝坊するなんて、オレ達って本当に気が合うよなぁ。

examples.en: If you have a habit of oversleeping, isn’t a morning job going to be too much for you?
examples.ja: 朝寝坊するクセがあるんだったら、朝早い仕事はムリなんじゃない？

examples.en: I’m a late riser but my sister is an early riser, she might be able to walk your dogs for you.
examples.ja: 私は朝寝坊だが、妹は私と違って早起きだから、君の犬の散歩に行けるかもしれないよ。

4861.meaning_mnemonic: Remember 寝坊 and how it means <kanji>oversleep</kanji>? Someone who oversleeps in the <kanji>morning</kanji> is someone who's a <vocabulary>late riser</vocabulary>.
4861.reading_mnemonic: The reading is the vocab words 朝 and 寝坊 put together into one. So long as you know them separately you should know them together too!

examples.en: It's open for business today, isn’t it, even though it's Sunday.
examples.ja: 今日は日曜日なのに営業中なんですね。

examples.en: I asked you not to call me when the shop is open.
examples.ja: 営業中に電話しないでって言ったじゃない。

examples.en: It's unthinkable for a top-class host to lean on their elbow in front of customers during business hours.
examples.ja: 営業中にお客さんの前でヒジをつくなんて、一流のホストだったらありえないよ。

4862.meaning_mnemonic: Remember how 営業 means "business"? Well, if you're in the <kanji>middle</kanji> of running a business, it means you're <vocabulary>open for business</vocabulary>.
4862.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help to know 営業 first as well.

examples.en: I parked my bike at the bicycle parking area at Kawasaki Station.
examples.ja: 川崎駅の自転車置き場に自転車を停めています。

examples.en: I was having a bit of trouble because there was no place to put this down.
examples.ja: 置き場がなくてちょっと困ってたんだ。

examples.en: We have a place for the towels under the sink, so help yourself after your shower.
examples.ja: 洗面台の下にタオル置き場があるから、シャワーの後勝手に取って使ってね。

4863.meaning_mnemonic:
置く is <kanji>to put down</kanji> something. So a <kanji>location</kanji> where you put something down is a <vocabulary>place to put something</vocabulary>.

置き場 often follows another word, signifying it's the designated area where that specific item should be stored or parked. For example, 自転車置き場.
4863.reading_mnemonic:
This word uses the kun'yomi readings. 置き comes from 置く, and you learned 場's reading with 場所, but here's a mnemonic to help you just in case:

You're looking for a <vocabulary>place to put something</vocabulary> that goes "<reading>baa</reading>" (ば). Your pet sheep won't stop baaing and it's getting annoying, so you want to put it somewhere. "Baa, baa," it bleats irritatingly as you search high and low for a good place to put it.

examples.en: I try to avoid taking a subjective view as much as possible.
examples.ja: できるだけ主観的な見方をしないように心がけています。

examples.en: His opinion is too subjective to be of use.
examples.ja: アイツの意見は主観的すぎて参考にならないよ。

examples.en: Looking at it subjectively, I think your point is spot on.
examples.ja: 主観的に見たら、その指摘は的を得てると思います。

examples.en: This may be a very subjective view, but to me, you work too much and should take time off sometime soon.
examples.ja: これはとても主観的な見方かもしれないけど、僕にとっては君は働き過ぎだと思うんだよね。近々休みを取った方がいいよ。

4864.meaning_mnemonic: 主観 is <kanji>subjectivity</kanji>. So when something moves towards subjectivity it is becoming <vocabulary>subjective</vocabulary>.
4864.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help if you know 主観.

examples.en: That's why I was reluctant to aid those two.
examples.ja: だからあの二人を援助することには気が進まなかったんだよ。

examples.en: I wonder what kind of benefits we would get as a company by assisting you.
examples.ja: あなたを援助することが会社にとってどんなプラスになるんでしょうか。

examples.en: The government prepared substantial funds to aid the disaster areas.
examples.ja: 政府は被災地を援助するために多額の資金を用意しました。

4865.meaning_mnemonic: You know that 援助 is <kanji>assistance</kanji> or <kanji>aid</kanji>. So the verb vocab version is <vocabulary>to assist</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>to aid</vocabulary>.
4865.reading_mnemonic: The reading is the same as 援助. It is also just the readings you learned with the kanji.

examples.en: Which sumo wrestler are you rooting for?
examples.ja: どっちの力士を応援してるの？

examples.en: All Tofugu employees are supporting team Japan.
examples.ja: トーフグ社員はみんな、日本代表を応援しています。

examples.en: I have no intention of refraining from supporting my favorite idol just because my grades have dropped.
examples.ja: 成績が落ちたからと言って、好きなアイドルを応援することを我慢する気はサラサラありません。

4866.meaning_mnemonic: 応援 is <kanji>aid</kanji> and <kanji>root for</kanji>, but for this verb the "root for" one is going to be more on the money. You can call this <vocabulary>to root for</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>to cheer on</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>to cheer for</vocabulary>.
4866.reading_mnemonic: The reading comes from 応援. It's also just the on'yomi readings you learned.

examples.en: I was supporting Takahashi Minami of AKB48.
examples.ja: 僕は、AKB４８の高橋みなみを応援していました。

examples.en: Who in the world was that campaign supporter who cheered fervently and loudly during the speech?
examples.ja: 応援演説で熱心に声を出してたあの応援者は、いったい誰だったんだ？

examples.en: I was chosen to lead the Tofugu cheerleading squad, but I had no idea what to do, so I asked my predecessor for advice.
examples.ja: トーフグ応援団の応援団長に選ばれたが、何をしていいか分からなかったので、前任者の応援を求めた。

4867.meaning_mnemonic: You must <kanji>respond</kanji> with <kanji>aid</kanji> in order to show your <vocabulary>support</vocabulary> for someone who needs it. You can usually show your support if you <vocabulary>root for</vocabulary> them.
4867.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: That guy with broad shoulders is the vice president of this country.
examples.ja: あのがっしりした広い肩の男が、この国の副大統領です。

examples.en: The vice president greeted the president, but the president completely ignored him.
examples.ja: 副大統領は大統領にあいさつしたが、完全に無視された。

examples.en: I think you should give it a try though. It may not be possible to become the president, but you could try going for vice president.
examples.ja: やってみるべきだと思うけど。大統領は無理でも、副大統領ぐらいなら狙えるんじゃない？

4868.meaning_mnemonic: You know about 大統領 (<kanji>president</kanji>), right? Well, this is the <kanji>vice</kanji> version of the president, aka the <vocabulary>vice president</vocabulary>.
4868.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It will help if you know the word 大統領 first, though.

examples.en: We proposed a new program to motivate our employees.
examples.ja: 私たちは、社員のやる気を上げるための新しいプログラムを提案しました。

examples.en: Yesterday, a newcomer proposed a great business model.
examples.ja: 昨日、新人が、素晴らしいビジネスモデルを提案してきた。

examples.en: I’d like to propose a new mutual fund to you today.
examples.ja: 本日は、新しい投資信託をご提案させて頂きたいと思います。

4869.meaning_mnemonic: You remember 提案, which means <kanji>proposition</kanji>? Make that into a verb and you have <vocabulary>to propose</vocabulary>.
4869.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: If there are well-motivated students, I'd like to support them.
examples.ja: やる気のある学生がいれば、支援してあげたいと思っています。

examples.en: I was really planning on supporting that project through crowdfunding, but I had a change of heart and decided not to support it.
examples.ja: 本気でクラウドファンディングでそのプロジェクトを支援するつもりでいたんですけど、気が変わって支援しないことにしたんです。

examples.en: I believe that supporting others also contributes to supporting oneself.
examples.ja: 僕は、他者を支援することは、自分自身を支援することにもつながると思っています。

4870.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Many tourists visit this town every year.
examples.ja: この町には毎年多くの観光客が訪れます。

examples.en: This tour is very popular among tourists.
examples.ja: このツアーは観光客にとても人気があります。

examples.en: The tourist had to pay $50 to get a doctor’s note in the U.S.
examples.ja: その観光客は、アメリカで医者の診断書をもらうために50ドルを支払わなければならなかった。

4871.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Will help to know 観光 as well.

examples.en: The actress's agent is skilled at relieving shoulder stiffness.
examples.ja: その女優のマネージャーは、肩こりをほぐすのが上手だ。

examples.en: It’s a lie that an actress with too kind of a heart won't succeed.
examples.ja: 優しすぎる女優は成功しないというのはウソです。

examples.en: "I don’t want to go to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry anymore. I want to be an actress." "Oh, don’t be ridiculous, Hermione."
examples.ja: 「ホグワーツ魔法魔術学校にはもう行きたくない。女優になりたいの。」「もう、馬鹿なこと言わないで。ハーマイオニーったら。」

4872.meaning_mnemonic: Remember how 男優 was "actor"? Well, I bet you can extrapolate what this one means because it now has <kanji>woman</kanji> in it. This is an <vocabulary>actress</vocabulary>.
4872.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Ernesto Che Guevara is a revolutionary born in Argentina.
examples.ja: エルネスト・チェ・ゲバラはアルゼンチン出身の革命家です。

examples.en: In April 1959, the Cuban revolutionary Fidel Castro arrived in New York.
examples.ja: 1959年4月、キューバ人革命家のフィデル・カストロが、ニューヨークにやってきました。

examples.en: If you want to be a revolutionary, first you need to be able to speak effectively.
examples.ja: 革命家になりたければ、まずは効果的な話し方を身につけないといけないよ。

examples.en: She fell in love with a passionate French revolutionary.
examples.ja: 彼女は情熱的なフランス人革命家と恋に落ちた。

4873.meaning_mnemonic: A person who lives in a revolution (革命) <kanji>house</kanji> is <vocabulary>a revolutionary</vocabulary>. They want government change! They want to take down the people in power!
4873.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Of course it will help to know 革命 already as well.

examples.en: I found a vintage leather jacket at a second-hand clothing shop.
examples.ja: 古着屋さんでビンテージものの革ジャンを見つけた。

examples.en: No way, I can't afford such an expensive leather jacket like that.
examples.ja: いや、あんな高い革ジャン買えるわけないじゃん。

examples.en: It started snowing, so Viet covered Koichi with his leather Jacket.
examples.ja: 雪が降ってきたので、ビエトは、コウイチに革ジャンを掛けてやった。

4874.meaning_mnemonic:
革 is <kanji>leather</kanji> and ジャン is short for ジャンパー (Jumper, like a jacket). So, put those together and you have a <vocabulary>leather jacket</vocabulary>.

This word is getting somewhat outdated. The trendier term now is レザージャケット.
4874.reading_mnemonic: The reading is the same as the vocab word 革, because this word is like two separate words put together (so it's treated as single words too, giving it that reading).

examples.en: Wow, it's such a small world isn't it? I never expected that my friend in Nagasaki prefecture is a friend of a friend of Koichi.
examples.ja: いやー、世の中って狭いもんですね。まさか私の長崎県の友人がコウイチの友人の友人だったとは。

examples.en: Just when I entered Nagasaki prefecture, my car engine stopped working.
examples.ja: 長崎県に入ったところで、車のエンジンが掛からなくなったんです。

examples.en: I am from Nagasaki prefecture and my family graves are all located there too.
examples.ja: 私は長崎県の出身で、家族の墓も全部そこにあります。

4875.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Long</kanji> <kanji>Cape</kanji> <kanji>Prefecture</kanji>. This will make more sense when you look at the reading. Hint: It's <vocabulary>Nagasaki Prefecture</vocabulary>.
4875.reading_mnemonic: The readings are 長 from 長い, normal 崎 and normal 県.

examples.en: Is that true?
examples.ja: それは本当ですか？

examples.en: I wonder if they will give you a million yen from this campaign?
examples.ja: キャンペーンで百万円くれるって、本当かな？

examples.en: I'm really bad at handwriting.
examples.ja: 本当に字が下手なのです。

4876.meaning_mnemonic: What is <kanji>real</kanji> is <kanji>right</kanji>. It is the <vocabulary>reality</vocabulary>. It is also the <vocabulary>truth</vocabulary>. Don't believe anything that isn't <vocabulary>real</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>true</vocabulary>.
4876.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Is this stone really important?
examples.ja: この石ころ、本当に大切？

examples.en: I'm worried if this map is truly accurate.
examples.ja: この地図が本当に正しいか不安です。

examples.en: Is this car seriously used?
examples.ja: この車、本当に中古なんですか？

4877.meaning_mnemonic: 本当 is <kanji>reality</kanji> or <kanji>truth</kanji> (level 5 vocab). If you add on に, this changes the word to an adverb, and we get <vocabulary>really</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>truly</vocabulary>. 本当に!
4877.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. It shares the reading with the level 5 本当 as well, but just has a particle on the end. Really!

examples.en: WaniKani is also called crabigator as its alias.
examples.ja: ワニカニは別名クラビゲーターとも呼ばれている。

examples.en: My name was called, but I just passed by as if I hadn't heard anything.
examples.ja: 名前を呼ばれたが、聞こえないふりをして通り過ぎた。

examples.en: I was a little sad to have reached the age where I can be called a middle-aged woman.
examples.ja: おばちゃんと呼ばれる年になってしまったことがちょっと悲しかった。

4878.meaning_mnemonic: If 呼ぶ is "to call" then this is something similar. This is when you are called by someone (and you're not doing the calling). This word is <vocabulary>to be called</vocabulary>.
4878.reading_mnemonic: The reading is shared with 呼ぶ, so remember that and you'll be able to read this too.

examples.en: Koichi finally showed up at the concert hall!
examples.ja: ついにコウイチがコンサート会場に姿を現したよ！

examples.en: The brave man defeated the monster that showed its true form.
examples.ja: 勇者は正体を現したモンスターをやっつけた。

examples.en: I knew that she would show her true colors in the end.
examples.ja: 彼女は最後には本性を現すと思ってたよ。

4879.meaning_mnemonic: This is the transitive version of 現れる (to appear), so rather than something appearing on its own, you’re making it appear. So this word means <vocabulary>to show</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>to reveal</vocabulary>, but it’s usually used in set phrases like 姿を現す (to show up) or 正体を現す (to reveal one's true nature).
4879.reading_mnemonic:
Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You learned that reading with 現れる, but here's a mnemonic to help you:

The monster under your bed decides <vocabulary>to show</vocabulary> you its true form. "You… <reading>are a wa</reading>lrus (あらわ)?" you ask, shocked. Evidently, the monster under your bed was actually just a walrus who got in one day when you left the window open. You feel silly for being scared of it for so long, but you're glad it finally showed itself to you.

examples.en: There is a park with a beautiful view near my house.
examples.ja: 家の近くに景色の良い公園があります。

examples.en: I love this landscape we can see from here.
examples.ja: ここから見る景色が大好きなんです。

examples.en: Do you want to take a detour today to see some different scenery than usual?
examples.ja: ちょっといつもと違った景色を見るために、今日は回り道をしてみない？

4880.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>scene</kanji>'s <kanji>color</kanji> is the <vocabulary>scenery</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>landscape</vocabulary>, and <vocabulary>view</vocabulary>. Looking good, scenery!
4880.reading_mnemonic:
You haven't learned either of these readings yet. Here's a mnemonic to help you remember them:

You're admiring the <vocabulary>scenery</vocabulary> and you notice key marks all over everything. You realize it's that girl who keys everything and you say to yourself <reading>kay she key</reading>ed (けしき) that, <reading>kay she key</reading>ed (けしき) this.

examples.en: Was there such an inn here?
examples.ja: こんな宿、ここにあったっけ？

examples.en: We still haven’t decided on a hotel yet.
examples.ja: 宿がまだ決まってないんだよ。

examples.en: This is a very famous inn.
examples.ja: ここはすごく有名な宿なんです。

4881.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>lodge</kanji> is a form of <vocabulary>lodging</vocabulary>. It is also considered to be an <vocabulary>inn</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>hotel</vocabulary>.
4881.reading_mnemonic: <reading>Yah do</reading> (やど) what you must to get <vocabulary>lodging</vocabulary>s for the night. Whether that's an <vocabulary>inn</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>hotel</vocabulary> or whatever. <reading>Yah do</reading> what you gotta do.

examples.en: I found one mistake!
examples.ja: 間違いを一つ見つけたよ！

examples.en: This is unmistakable, isn't it?
examples.ja: これは間違いないね！

examples.en: It was a mistake to ask you about Final Fantasy.
examples.ja: ファイナルファンタジーについて君に聞いたのが間違いだったよ。

examples.en: Expanding into new markets was not a mistake.
examples.ja: 新しい市場に参入したことは間違いじゃなかった。

4882.meaning_mnemonic: We waited an <kanji>interval of time</kanji>, and at each interval it was <kanji>different</kanji>. They're all supposed to be the same. Is there some kind of <vocabulary>mistake</vocabulary>?
4882.reading_mnemonic: Take the reading of 間 (ま from 間に合う) and 違う and you'll have the reading for this word too.

examples.en: I'll place this Tofugu doll on top of the shelf, okay?
examples.ja: このトーフグ人形は、あのたなの上に載せておきますね。

examples.en: It's not acceptable nowadays to put someone's address and phone number on the list without consent.
examples.ja: 同意なしに住所や電話番号をリストに載せるなんて、今時ありえないです。

examples.en: I’m a little uncomfortable publishing my own picture on the Internet.
examples.ja: 自分の写真をインターネットに載せるのには、ちょっと抵抗があります。

4883.meaning_mnemonic:
Remember how 載る is "to be placed on"? This one is <vocabulary>to place on something</vocabulary>, like a mug on a table. 載せる is transitive, and you know this because you do it your<reading>sel</reading>f (せる). Like 載る, 載せる also often refers to putting something in a written document or publication, so it can mean <vocabulary>to put on record</vocabulary>.

Note that 載せる is never used to refer to putting clothing or accessories on. That's 着る or 着ける respectively, which you've learned already.
4883.reading_mnemonic: The reading is shared with 載る, so as long as you remember that you can remember this.

examples.en: I went to a job interview for the weather agency.
examples.ja: 気象庁の仕事の面接を受けてきました。

examples.en: According to the announcement from the meteorological agency, it seems that an earthquake happened in Tokyo this morning.
examples.ja: 気象庁の発表では、今朝東京で地震があったようですよ。

examples.en: I thought I finally got my call through to the weather agency, but they hung up on me. Unbelievable.
examples.ja: やっと気象庁に電話が繋がったと思ったら、切られたんだよ。ありえなくね？

examples.en: The Japan Meteorological Agency provides information related to disaster prevention, weather, traffic safety, industrial updates, daily life, and environmental data. All while contributing to the safety and well-being of people.
examples.ja: 気象庁は、防災気象情報、交通安全情報、産業情報、生活情報、地球環境に関する情報などを提供し、人々の安全と生活を支えています。

4884.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>energy</kanji> <kanji>phenomenon</kanji> <kanji>agency</kanji> sounds like something that could be really cool but it's really just the <vocabulary>weather agency</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>meteorological agency</vocabulary>. Nothing shady going on here.
4884.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Do you think ghosts really exist?
examples.ja: お化けって本当に居ると思いますか？

examples.en: Wait, that celebrity is still around? I wonder how old she is now.
examples.ja: え？あの芸能人ってまだ居たの？今何才なんだろう？

examples.en: Our cat is usually in our bedroom upstairs.
examples.ja: うちの猫は大抵二階の寝室に居るんです。

4885.meaning_mnemonic:
Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means <kanji>alive</kanji> and the verb version means <vocabulary>to exist</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>to be</vocabulary>, for anything that is alive and moving, like people and animals. 

The kanji isn't used too often for this word, so when you're writing just use the kana. But you'll see the kanji used sometimes so it's important to be able to recognize it!
4885.reading_mnemonic: Do you know the word いる? This is the kanji version! If you've been studying Japanese up to this point you probably already know that word. You can associate these two things together into one and remember the reading at the same time!

examples.en: Are there any differences in the structure of Japanese and American society?
examples.ja: 日本社会とアメリカ社会の構造に違いはありますか。

examples.en: I wonder what kind of structure is inside that person's brain.
examples.ja: あの人の脳内、一体どんな構造をしてるんだろうね。

examples.en: I’ll teach you guys essay structure and rules today.
examples.ja: 今日はエッセイの構造とルールについて授業をします。

4886.meaning_mnemonic: First you have to <kanji>set up</kanji> the <vocabulary>structure</vocabulary> of something to <kanji>create</kanji> it. This structure is important for the creation of everything, otherwise it would just fall apart.
4886.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: The man, though staggering, began to slowly walk once again.
examples.ja: 男はよろめきながらも、再びゆっくりと歩き始めた。

examples.en: I didn't think I would end up visiting this place again.
examples.ja: この地を再び訪れることになるとは思ってもいなかったよ。

examples.en: The next morning, the monster appeared again.
examples.ja: 次の朝、怪物は再び現れた。

4887.meaning_mnemonic:
This is the adverb version of 再, so it shares the meaning <vocabulary>again</vocabulary> and also has the meaning <vocabulary>once again</vocabulary>.

Note that this word is somewhat formal and literary.
4887.reading_mnemonic:
Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you:

<vocabulary>Once again</vocabulary>, you have to say "<reading>Who</reading>? <reading>Ta</reading>-<reading>ta</reading>!" (ふたた). That's because people you don't know keep trying to talk to you, <vocabulary>again</vocabulary> and again. Whenever this happens you say "Who? Ta-ta!" again and run away.

examples.en: My cousin’s wedding will take place the month after next.
examples.ja: 再来月にいとこの式があるんです。

examples.en: My son who went to fight in the war will finally come back the month after next.
examples.ja: 戦争に行った息子がようやく再来月帰ってくるんです。

examples.en: I can take a week-long vacation the month after next, so wanna go somewhere together?
examples.ja: 再来月に一週間の休暇が取れるんだけど、どこか一緒にいかない？

4888.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>next month</kanji> (来月) isn't enough... one more next month, please. Let's do it <kanji>again</kanji>. That month is the <vocabulary>month after next</vocabulary>.
4888.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: By the year after next, the economy should have improved.
examples.ja: 再来年には景気もよくなっているでしょう。

examples.en: I plan to return to my family's home in Japan the year after next.
examples.ja: 再来年に日本の実家に帰るつもりです。

examples.en: Shouldn't we propose a two-year contract that lasts until the year after next?
examples.ja: 再来年まで継続する二年契約を提案するべきではないでしょうか。

4889.meaning_mnemonic: You have <kanji>next year</kanji> (来年), but then you do a year <kanji>again</kanji>. That's the <vocabulary>year after next</vocabulary>.
4889.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: The sports festival is not this week, but the week after next.
examples.ja: 運動会は今週じゃなくて再来週だよ。

examples.en: What's the plan for the week after next?
examples.ja: 再来週の予定ってどんな感じ？

examples.en: Would it be possible to reschedule lunch for the week after next?
examples.ja: ランチ、再来週にリスケできないかな？

4890.meaning_mnemonic: You know how 来週 is <kanji>next week</kanji>? Well, if you do next week again, you have the <vocabulary>week after next</vocabulary>.
4890.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: I heard the police have reopened the investigation.
examples.ja: 警察は捜査を再開したそうだよ。

examples.en: The conditions for resumption of war have been fully met.
examples.ja: 戦争の再開条件は十分に満たされている。

examples.en: Negotiations between Koichi and Viet will be reopened soon.
examples.ja: コウイチとビエトの交渉は、近々再開される予定だ。

4891.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Again</kanji> it is <kanji>open</kanji>ing. This is the <vocabulary>reopening</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>resumption</vocabulary>.
4891.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just don't forget that extra い!

examples.en: This is a major project aimed at national reconstruction.
examples.ja: これは国家再建をかけた一大プロジェクトです。

examples.en: To rebuild this building, we will need to secure funding first.
examples.ja: このビルの再建には、まずは資金を作らなくてはいけません。

examples.en: Rebuilding the disaster-stricken areas is top priority now.
examples.ja: 今は被災地の再建が最優先です。

examples.en: He worked longer hours than he was supposed to every day until he rebuilt his struggling company.
examples.ja: 経営が苦しくなった会社を再建するまで、彼は毎日規定よりも長い時間働いた。

4892.meaning_mnemonic:
<kanji>Again</kanji> you <kanji>build</kanji> it. This is <vocabulary>rebuilding</vocabulary>.

再建 is a formal word that refers to the act of rebuilding something that has deteriorated or been lost, whether it's a physical structure like a building or an organization, or a part of the body in the context of medical procedures.
4892.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just don't forget that extra い!

examples.en: Perhaps we should look into this again.
examples.ja: この件については再度検討した方がいいかもね。

examples.en: The project was shelved for the second time.
examples.ja: 計画は再度たな上げになってしまった。

examples.en: I’m sorry to trouble you, but could you please check again to be sure?
examples.ja: お手数ですが、念のため再度確認していただけないでしょうか。

examples.en: They may bring forward a petition against our land reclamation project again.
examples.ja: 相手は、埋め立て計画に反対する請願書を再度持ってくるかもしれませんよ。

4893.meaning_mnemonic:
<kanji>Again</kanji> with that <kanji>occurrence</kanji>? That occurrence has now happened <vocabulary>again</vocabulary>.

Note that this word is relatively formal.
4893.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. Just remember that there's a い hiding in there!

examples.en: Because there are so many young people around me, it's stimulating for me too.
examples.ja: 周りに若い人が多いので、私も刺激を受けています。

examples.en: Don't provoke Koichi anymore. There is no knowing what he will do next.
examples.ja: コウイチをこれ以上刺激しないで。何しでかすか分からないよ。

examples.en: I met her, but we didn't really hit it off. For me, I'd rather have a woman who is a little more exciting.
examples.ja: 彼女には会ったんだけど、お互いにいまいちピンと来なかったんだよな。俺としては、もうちょっと刺激的な女性の方がいいっていうかさ。

4894.meaning_mnemonic: You have all these little <kanji>stab</kanji>s that are very <kanji>fierce</kanji> on you. They tingle like crazy. This is quite the <vocabulary>stimulation</vocabulary> on your body. *tingle tingle tingle.*
4894.reading_mnemonic:
This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You learned this reading of 刺 already with 名刺, but here's a mnemonic in case it's not coming to you:

<vocabulary>Stimulation</vocabulary> for your <reading>shee</reading>p (し) is the best way to make its wool grow faster. All the woolliest sheep are stimulated daily with massages and exercise, if you think about. Sheep need stimulation!

examples.en: Oh, are we going to be sticking these fruits on skewers?
examples.ja: え、このフルーツをクシに刺すんですか？

examples.en: I've been stung by a black hornet before.
examples.ja: 黒いスズメバチに刺されたことがあります。

examples.en: I finished off a fly with a fork.
examples.ja: フォークでハエにトドメを刺しました。

4895.meaning_mnemonic:
Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb.

The kanji itself means <kanji>stab</kanji> so the verb vocab version is <vocabulary>to stab something</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>to pierce something</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>to sting something</vocabulary>.

This is a transitive verb, meaning that you're the one doing the stabbing... Should I be afraid of you?
4895.reading_mnemonic:
Since this vocab word is made up of a single kanji, it uses the kun'yomi reading. Luckily you learned that reading with the kanji! Still, here's a mnemonic just in case:

If you're going <vocabulary>to stab something</vocabulary>, use a <reading>saw</reading> (さ). It may seem more difficult to stab something with a saw at first, but when you see the damage, plus how hard it is to get back out, you'll realize saws are the ideal stabbing tool.

examples.en: I've ordered new business cards.
examples.ja: 新しい名刺を注文しました。

examples.en: Come to think of it, we need to make business cards for the new hires, don't we?
examples.ja: そういえば、新人の名刺を作る必要がありますね。

examples.en: I received a business card from the president of that company.
examples.ja: あの会社の社長さんから名刺をもらいました。

4896.meaning_mnemonic: Take your <kanji>name</kanji> and <kanji>stab</kanji> someone with it... using your <vocabulary>business card</vocabulary>. Your business card has your name on it. Also, you "stab" it at people who are willing to take it and read it. Not a real stab, but a metaphorical.
4896.reading_mnemonic:
This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You haven't learned this reading for 刺 yet, so here's a mnemonic to help you:

After doing business in Japan, you'll have so many <vocabulary>business card</vocabulary>s you can count them like <reading>shee</reading>p (し) when you're trying to get to sleep. One business card, two business cards… See them leaping over the sheep fence as you begin to nod off.

examples.en: Did God really create human beings?
examples.ja: 神様は本当に人間を創造したんですか。

examples.en: We're always required to create something new.
examples.ja: 常に新たな創造を求められます。

examples.en: I witnessed the Creation... okay that's a lie.
examples.ja: 私は、天地創造を目の当たりにしました...というのはウソです。

4897.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Create</kanji>! <kanji>Create</kanji>! If you do this, you are doing <vocabulary>creation</vocabulary>.
4897.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: It’s so disappointing that he is lacking in originality.
examples.ja: 彼が独創性に欠けていることは非常に残念です。

examples.en: The more creative your idea is, the more people come out against it.
examples.ja: アイディアが独創的であれば独創的であるほど、反対する人も多いよね。

examples.en: WaniKani is President Koichi's original creation.
examples.ja: ワニカニはコウイチ社長の独創です。

4898.meaning_mnemonic:
You are <kanji>alone</kanji> in what you are able to <kanji>create</kanji>. Nobody else can create like you. So what you create is your own <vocabulary>original creation</vocabulary>.

独創 refers to the act of <vocabulary>creating something original</vocabulary>, or the resulting creation itself. This word is quite formal, and generally used as 独創的 (original) or 独創性 (originality).
4898.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Koichi intends to establish the University of Tofugu before he dies.
examples.ja: コウイチは、死ぬまでにトーフグ大学を創立するつもりだ。

examples.en: Today is the anniversary of the founding of Tofugu.
examples.ja: 今日はトーフグの創立記念日なんです。

examples.en: Do you know who the founders of WaniKani are?
examples.ja: ワニカニの創立者が誰かはご存知ですよね？

examples.en: I’ve missed my train and I’m running late for my company’s anniversary event.
examples.ja: 電車に乗り遅れて、会社の創立記念のイベントに遅れそうだ。

4899.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Create</kanji> it and <kanji>stand</kanji> it up. This is your <vocabulary>establishment</vocabulary>, your <vocabulary>founding</vocabulary>.
4899.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: President Koichi offered us words of encouragement.
examples.ja: コウイチ社長から、激励の言葉をいただきました。

examples.en: Before the JLPT test, my teacher gave me a pep talk.
examples.ja: 日本語能力検定試験の前に、先生が激励してくれました。

examples.en: After the TV show, hundreds of calls offering encouragement came pouring in for hours.
examples.ja: テレビ番組が放映された後、何百にも及ぶ激励の電話が、数時間に渡って掛かってきた。

4900.meaning_mnemonic:
If someone is <kanji>fierce</kanji> when they <kanji>encourage</kanji> you, that's some <vocabulary>strong encouragement</vocabulary>! 

This word is kind of formal, and using it will really communicate your appreciation for the <vocabulary>encouragement</vocabulary> someone gives you. Even if they just tossed a casual 頑張れ your way, calling that 激励 will make it sound like some of the strongest, warmest encouragement you've ever gotten.
4900.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: I'm not good at encouraging others.
examples.ja: 私は人を励ますのが苦手だ。

examples.en: Thank you for always encouraging me.
examples.ja: いつも励ましてくれてありがとう。

examples.en: It's hard to cheer up someone who's depressed.
examples.ja: 落ち込んでいる人を励ますのは難しい。

4901.meaning_mnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means <kanji>encourage</kanji> and the verb vocab version is <vocabulary>to encourage someone</vocabulary> (or <vocabulary>to encourage</vocabulary>).
4901.reading_mnemonic: Think about encouraging a <reading>hag</reading> (はげ). She needs encouragement because she's a hag, and nobody likes her much because of that.

examples.en: I try to believe only in the good things from fortune telling.
examples.ja: 占いは、良いことだけ信じるようにしています。

examples.en: Fortune telling told me to turn on the radio at six every morning this week, so I set my alarm for 5:55.
examples.ja: 占いで、今週は毎朝六時にラジオを掛けるように言われたから、五時五十五分に目覚まし時計を掛けているんです。

examples.en: According to the stars, Fugu and I aren’t supposed to have so much chemistry between us.
examples.ja: 星占いによると、フグと私ってあまり相性が良くないみたいなんだよね。

4902.meaning_mnemonic: Although this has a い on the end it's tricky and not an adjective. The kanji is <kanji>fortune</kanji>, and the vocab word is <vocabulary>fortune telling</vocabulary>.
4902.reading_mnemonic: I'm going to do some <vocabulary>fortune telling</vocabulary> on you... hmmm... I see... ohhhh... Looks like you'll be living on <reading>Uranu</reading>s (うらな) in your near future, that will be $50. What a dumb fortune telling for $50, you definitely won't be living there, unless he meant your butt, then maybe.

examples.en: I heard Tofugu is thinking of cornering the bacon market.
examples.ja: トーフグがベーコン市場を買い占めるつもりだと聞きましたよ。

examples.en: The sales of President Koichi's candid photos account for 80% of Tofugu's total sales.
examples.ja: コウイチ社長の生写真の売り上げが、トーフグの全売り上げの80%を占めるんです。

examples.en: Today's party venue was occupied with women who are around 30 years old.
examples.ja: 今日のパーティー会場はアラサーの女性で占められていました。

examples.en: If the opposition has the majority, there's no helping it.
examples.ja: 反対者が過半数を占めてるんじゃ、仕方ないね。

4903.meaning_mnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means <kanji>occupy</kanji> so the verb version is <vocabulary>to occupy</vocabulary>.
4903.reading_mnemonic: What is it you want <vocabulary>to occupy</vocabulary> most in the whole, entire world? Your own flock of <reading>shee</reading>p (し). Also, a fortune teller (this kanji also means fortune, remember) told you that if you occupy her sheep, you'll have good luck! Gotta do as she says!

examples.en: In my family’s case, my father monopolizes the television.
examples.ja: うちの家族の場合は、父がテレビを独占しています。

examples.en: Until then, it was a monopolistic business by a single provider.
examples.ja: それまでは、一つのプロバイダによる独占的な事業でした。

examples.en: That company is under investigation for suspected violations of antitrust laws.
examples.ja: あの会社は独占禁止法違反の疑いで調査を受けている。

4904.meaning_mnemonic: You are <kanji>alone</kanji> in what you <kanji>occupy</kanji>. Nobody but you occupies it. You have a <vocabulary>monopoly</vocabulary>. You <vocabulary>monopolize</vocabulary> it.
4904.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Let's mark it here so we don't get lost.
examples.ja: 道にまよわないように、ここに印をつけておこう。

examples.en: As a token of our friendship, I give you this.
examples.ja: 友情の印にこれをあげるよ。

examples.en: I like putting a heart mark at the end of letters.
examples.ja: 私は手紙の最後にハートの印を付けるのが好きです。

4905.meaning_mnemonic: The kanji and the word are almost exactly the same. This word means <vocabulary>mark</vocabulary>.
4905.reading_mnemonic: You see a beautiful woman in front of you. She shows you a <vocabulary>mark</vocabulary> on a piece of paper. It's a mark that tells you she's Russian (しるし)!

examples.en: I heard that the first impression wasn’t very good.
examples.ja: 第一印象はあまりいいものではなかったらしいです。

examples.en: My first impression of you was a self-assertive person, but you were totally different, right?
examples.ja: 第一印象では我の強そうな人だなぁと思っていたんですが、全然違っていましたね。

examples.en: We were all taught that an operator is the first impression that a caller has of our company.
examples.ja: オペレーターは、電話をかけてくださったお客様にとって、会社の 第一印象になるということを教えられました。

4906.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>The first</kanji> (第一) <kanji>phenomenon</kanji> is what's <kanji>seal</kanji>ed into your head. This is your <vocabulary>first impression</vocabulary> of something.
4906.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: I need to deliver this pizza to the customer within thirty minutes.
examples.ja: このピザをお客さんに三十分以内に届ける必要があるんです。

examples.en: I’ll deliver my computer and external hard drive to you tonight.
examples.ja: 今夜お前のところに俺のパソコンと外付けハードディスクを届けるよ。

examples.en: Koichi always says he wants to deliver love to WaniKani users.
examples.ja: コウイチはいつもワニカニユーザーに愛を届けたいと言っています。

examples.en: Have you already notified the ward office about the birth of your baby?
examples.ja: 赤ちゃんの出生はもう区役所に届けましたか？

4907.meaning_mnemonic: 届く is "to be delivered." This word is when you're doing the actual delivering, making it <vocabulary>to deliver</vocabulary>. You can remember this because you <reading>care</reading> (ける) about the package so much that you deliver it yourself, thus doing the action of delivering it!
4907.reading_mnemonic: The reading is the same as 届く and you can use that to deliver the memory to your brain.

examples.en: Why do you discriminate?
examples.ja: どうして差別するんですか？

examples.en: Have you ever been discriminated against by someone?
examples.ja: 誰かに差別されたことはありますか。

examples.en: I think many people unconsciously discriminate against foreigners.

examples.en: What do you think what would happen if I didn’t obey his orders?

examples.en: Even if you're dissatisfied, you should still obey the rules. Then, you can work to correct what's wrong.

4912.meaning_mnemonic: Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means <kanji>obey</kanji> so the verb vocab version is <vocabulary>to obey</vocabulary>.
4912.reading_mnemonic:
Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: 

I am going <vocabulary>to obey</vocabulary> you. I think your order is a bit of <reading>shit が</reading> (したが), I'll do it and obey you. 

(Little side note, did you know が in the middle of a sentence can mean "but" in Japanese? Think of it as that meaning here.)

examples.en: Employees here seem to be more optimistic than their Osaka-branch counterparts.
examples.ja: ここの従業員たちは、大阪支店の従業員たちより楽観的なようだ。

examples.en: The number of employees working for this company is approximately one hundred.

examples.en: The content of the work to be engaged in will be determined through consultation with the company.

examples.en: Including holidays and such, the entire period of employment is referred to as the "employment period."
examples.ja: 休日などを含め、雇われていた全期間のことを「従業期間」と言います。

4913.meaning_mnemonic:
You must <kanji>obey</kanji> your <kanji>business</kanji>. When you're in this situation, you’re <vocabulary>engaging in work</vocabulary>.

This is most commonly used in the compounds 従業員 (employee) and 従業者 (worker). You might also come across other forms, such as 従業する, but these are generally found in formal writing.

examples.en: Unlike the tattoo inks used up until now, new tattoo inks that disappear in about a year have been developed.

examples.en: Conventionally, first year employees have been given zero paid holidays in this company.
examples.ja: 従来、一年目の新入社員はこの会社では有給休暇は一日ももらえません。

4914.meaning_mnemonic:
You've <kanji>obey</kanji>ed all that has <kanji>come</kanji> <vocabulary>up to now</vocabulary>. That's because it's the <vocabulary>conventional</vocabulary> way of doing things, and it's what's <vocabulary>conventionally</vocabulary> expected of you.

This word is a relatively formal way to talk about how things have been up to now. It's commonly used with の to modify a noun or phrase, or as an adverb.
4914.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

4915.meaning_mnemonic: <kanji>Restore</kanji> what you <kanji>learn</kanji>ed with <vocabulary>review</vocabulary>s. That's what you do on WaniKani, right?
4915.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Naoko has regained consciousness!

examples.en: Our Internet connection hasn’t recovered yet.

4916.meaning_mnemonic: Many <kanji>times</kanji> you <kanji>restore</kanji> something. You do this over and over for the <vocabulary>recovery</vocabulary> of this thing.

examples.en: She takes more sick time than the other coworkers, so it’s suspicious whether she’s really sick or not.
examples.ja: 彼女は同僚に比べて病欠が多いし、本当に病気なのか怪しいよね。

4919.meaning_mnemonic: This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of <kanji>suspicious</kanji>? Also <vocabulary>suspicious</vocabulary>!
4919.reading_mnemonic: Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. Just think of our artist Aya, she's super suspicious and shady!

examples.en: It was such a strange mystery, wasn't it?
examples.ja: とんだ怪事件だったね。

examples.en: Koichi's "The Mysterious Affair at the Tofugu Office" is a masterpiece that is as good as Edgar Allan Poe's "The Mystery of Marie Roget.”
examples.ja: コウイチの書いた「トーフグオフィスの怪事件」は、エドガー・アラン・ポーの「マリー・ロジェエの怪事件」とならぶ、素晴らしい作品だ。

examples.en: Even Holmes wouldn’t be able to find a clue to that mystery.
examples.ja: ホームズでさえもその怪事件の糸口を見つけることはできないだろう。

4920.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.ja: 夏になるとなぜか怪談が聞きたくなる。

examples.en: I heard that a movie based on a famous ghost story would be produced soon.
examples.ja: 今度、有名な怪談を元にした映画が制作されるそうです。

4921.meaning_mnemonic: If you have a <kanji>suspicious</kanji> <kanji>talk</kanji>, you're talking about something that may or may not be real. One of those things you could be discussing is a <vocabulary>ghost story</vocabulary>.
4921.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: When the store opened, everyone ran towards the sale items, each of them focused on themselves.
examples.ja: お店が開くと、みんな我も我もとセール品を目掛けて走り出した。

examples.en: During my childhood, there were many things I could enjoy wholeheartedly, forgetting myself.
examples.ja: 子供時代は、我を忘れて夢中で楽しめることがたくさんあった

examples.en: When I came to my senses, it had become an irreversible situation.
examples.ja: 我に返った時には、取り返しのつかないことになっていた。

examples.en: I hate how he acts as if he doesn’t care.
examples.ja: 我関せずって感じのアイツの態度、超嫌なんだけど。

4922.meaning_mnemonic:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.

我 is an old-fashioned pronoun and isn't commonly used outside of set phrases like 我を忘れる (to forget oneself or be utterly absorbed) or 我に返る (to come back to reality or return to one's senses).
4922.reading_mnemonic:
Since this word is made up of a single kanji, it probably uses the kun'yomi reading. You did not learn this reading, so here's a mnemonic to help you remember: 

It is <vocabulary>I</vocabulary>! Due to my ego, I love the Wii and no other gaming device. I love playing all the Wii-<reading>ware</reading> (われ) that's available, and everything else sucks.

examples.en: I was being chased by a shark and swam for dear life.
examples.ja: 私はサメに追いかけられて、無我夢中で泳ぎました。

examples.en: Koichi finally reached a state of selflessness.
examples.ja: コウイチはついに無我の境地に達した。

examples.en: If you are not kind to yourself, you will not be kind to others. So, taking care of yourself is what selflessness is all about.
examples.ja: 自分に優しくない人は、他人に優しくなれない。すなわち、自分を大切にすることこそが、無我なのである。

4923.meaning_mnemonic:
There is <kanji>not</kanji> any of <kanji>I</kanji>. It is all about everyone else. It is all about <vocabulary>selflessness</vocabulary>.

This word is commonly used in the phrase 無我夢中 (total absorption).
4923.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: It's young people that are responsible for Japan's future.
examples.ja: 日本の未来を担うのは若者たちです。

examples.en: Tofugu aims to foster the development of individuals who will shape the future of society.
examples.ja: トーフグは、これからの社会を担う人材の育成を目指しています。

examples.en: My company’s profits soared 70% over last year and I played an important part in achieving that.
examples.ja: 我が社の純利益は前年比で70％も上昇したが、それを達成するために私が重要な役割を担ったんだ。

examples.en: The president is supposed to be responsible for articulating the company's vision, right? However, in our case, our president is playing the role of an air conditioner that chills everyone with puns during a hot summer.
examples.ja: 会社のビジョンを明確にするのを担うのが社長だろ？でもうちの社長が担ってるのは、暑い夏にダジャレでみんなを寒くするエアコンディションの役目なんだ。

4924.meaning_mnemonic:
担ぐ is more like when you're carrying something physical. 担う is when you carry a responsibility, which is why this word means <vocabulary>to assume responsibility</vocabulary>. You can remember this because <reading>YOU</reading> (う) are responsible for this. You assume this responsibility.

Note that 担う is generally used with another word that specifies the responsibility, like 役割を担う (assume a role) or 未来を担う (bear the future).
4924.reading_mnemonic: What is your responsibility? To raise this girl named <reading>Nina</reading> (にな).

examples.en: Please shake it well before drinking.
examples.ja: よく振ってから飲んでください。

examples.en: It was cute when the baby waved goodbye.
examples.ja: 赤ちゃんがバイバイと手を振るのが可愛かったです。

examples.en: My dog always wags its tail vigorously when it sees me.
examples.ja: うちの犬は、私を見るといつも思いっきりシッポを振るんですよ。

examples.en: Koichi nodded his head, but Viet shook his head.
examples.ja: コウイチは首をたてに振ったが、ビエトは首を横に振った。

examples.en: "I can’t believe he broke up with me." "You cheated on him. You had it coming."
examples.ja: 「彼に振られたなんて信じられない。」「あんた、浮気してたんでしょ。自業自得だよ。」

4925.meaning_mnemonic:
Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means <kanji>shake</kanji> and this verb is transitive, meaning that you're shaking something. So this verb means <vocabulary>to shake something</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>to wave something</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>to swing something</vocabulary>. You'll often see it paired with 手, as in 手を振る, meaning "to wave one's hand" or, as we'd usually say in English, simply "to wave".

This word can also be used when you shake someone off in the less physical way, as in <vocabulary>to break up with someone</vocabulary>.
4925.reading_mnemonic:
Since this word consists of a kanji with hiragana attached, you can bet that it will use the kun'yomi reading. You didn't learn that reading with this kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you:

Someone is trying <vocabulary>to shake something</vocabulary>. And unfortunately, that something is you. The most unfortunate thing here is that you're totally <reading>full</reading> (ふる), and you throw up because of the shaking (and you're full, gross!).

examples.en: I like feeling the vibration of an engine in a car.
examples.ja: 車の中で、エンジンの振動を感じるのが好きなんです。

examples.en: Sound is caused by vibrations in the air, and low-pitched sounds have slower air vibrations.
examples.ja: 音は空気の振動で、低い音は空気の振動が遅いんです。

examples.en: Have you ever experienced feeling the vibrations from someone sitting next to you on the couch when they pass gas?
examples.ja: ソファに座っている時、となりにいる人がオナラをした振動が伝わってきた経験はありませんか？

examples.en: Then suddenly, there was a sensation as if my whole body was vibrating intensely.
examples.ja: すると突然、体全体がビリビリと振動するような感覚があった。

4926.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>move</kanji>ment that has to do with <kanji>shake</kanji>s is <vocabulary>vibration</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>oscillation</vocabulary>.
4926.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: It seems like Ichiro is in a slump this season, wouldn't you say?
examples.ja: イチローは今季は不振なようだね。

examples.en: I've been experiencing a loss of appetite recently.
examples.ja: 最近、食欲不振が続いてるんです。

examples.en: I'm feeling down due to the business' poor performance, and it's causing me to lose my appetite.
examples.ja: 業績不振で落ちこんでいて、食欲不振になっているんです。

examples.en: My CD was suffering from a slump in sales for a little while, but since being introduced on the radio, sales are rising again this month.
examples.ja: 私のCDはしばらく売上不振に苦しんでいたが、ラジオで紹介されてから今月は売上げが上昇しています。

4927.meaning_mnemonic:
If something does <kanji>not</kanji> <kanji>shake</kanji>, it’s probably in <vocabulary>a slump</vocabulary>. If nothing’s shaking, things must be <vocabulary>sluggish</vocabulary>.

不振 is used for times when things are slower or worse than usual. For example, 業績不振 is when a business isn’t doing as well as it usually does, and 食欲不振 is when you don't feel like eating as much as you normally would.
4927.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: That professor's son backs up Koichi quite a lot, yeah?
examples.ja: あの教授の息子、ずい分コウイチに肩入れしてるよね。

examples.en: I received instruction on piano teaching methods from a professor at the music university.

4929.meaning_mnemonic:
If you <kanji>teach</kanji> and <kanji>instruct</kanji>, then you may be some kind of <vocabulary>professor</vocabulary>. And a professor's work is… <vocabulary>teaching</vocabulary>!

教授 usually means a university professor, but it can also refer to other kinds of expert instruction in a formal context. You can even use it in phrases like ご教授ありがとうございます to show respect for the expertise of someone of higher status.
4929.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: That is not directly related.
examples.ja: それは直接関係ありません。

examples.en: In the end, what was the direct cause?
examples.ja: 結局、直接の原因は何だったんですか？

examples.en: I'll meet the person directly and see for myself.
examples.ja: 直接会って、確かめてみるよ。

examples.en: I heard that you two ate my bacon directly from him.
examples.ja: 君と彼が僕のベーコンを食べたって話は、彼から直接聞いたんだよ。

4930.meaning_mnemonic:
Remember how 直 can also mean "direct?" Well, if you <kanji>direct</kanji>ly <kanji>adjoin</kanji> two things, their connection will become <vocabulary>direct</vocabulary> too. Nothing will stand between them!

That said, 直接 isn't limited to physical contact. In fact, it's more often used when someone does something without going through a middle step or person, whether it's in communication, action, or connection. For example, if you say 直接聞いた (I heard it directly), it means you got the info straight from the source.

examples.ja: 消費税は間接税です。

examples.en: I’m looking for soft, romantic, indirect lighting for our bedroom.
examples.ja: 寝室用の落ち着いた感じのロマンチックな間接照明を探しているんです。

4931.meaning_mnemonic: After an <kanji>interval of time</kanji> it will <kanji>adjoin</kanji>, but not right away. That is because it was being <vocabulary>indirect</vocabulary>.
4931.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: The interviewer for the interview this time was a woman.
examples.ja: 今回の面接の面接官は女性でした。

examples.en: The location of the interview will be at our office in Portland. Is that okay?
examples.ja: 面接する場所はポートランドのオフィスになりますが、よろしいですか？

examples.en: The secondary exam is a speaking test in the form of an interview.
examples.ja: 二次試験は面接形式のスピーキングテストです。

4932.meaning_mnemonic:
Our <kanji>face</kanji>s have <kanji>adjoin</kanji>ed in this one room to talk. You did the telephone interview where you didn't show the face of your face. Now you're showing it, so we can begin the real <vocabulary>interview</vocabulary>.

面接 generally refers to a <vocabulary>job interview</vocabulary> or an <vocabulary>oral examination</vocabulary>. For conversations between media professionals and people of public interest, インタビュー is used instead.
4932.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Therefore, this medication became known to the people.
examples.ja: 故に、この薬は人々に知られるようになったのです。

examples.en: As a consequence of being good-looking, people tend to only look at my face. I used to dislike it, but now I accept it as the fate that comes with being a beautiful woman.
examples.ja: 私は美人が故に顔ばかり見られます。以前は嫌だったんですが、今は美人が故の宿命だと思って受け入れています。

examples.en: "Why do you humans suffer?" "It is because of love that humans must suffer."
examples.ja: 「何が故にソナタたち人間は苦しむのじゃ？」「愛故に人は苦しまねばならぬのだ」

examples.en: I was repeatedly late without permission and consequently my vacation days were cut short.
examples.ja: 度重なる無断遅刻故に、 休暇日数が減らされてしまった。

4933.meaning_mnemonic:
You learned that 故 means reason. Basically, whatever comes before 故に in a statement is going to be the reason for something that comes after. So 故に works like <vocabulary>therefore</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>consequently</vocabulary>. It can also be translated as "because" or other similar conjunctions depending on the context.

Also keep in mind that 故に is mainly used in formal contexts, like in academic writing or politicians' speeches — just like "therefore" in English.
4933.reading_mnemonic:
By knowing the word 故 you'll know the reading for this word too! Here's a mnemonic in case you need a reminder, though:

You're using WaniKani, <vocabulary>therefore</vocabulary> you're studying kanji and vocab. Whose fault is it? It's WaniKani's fault! But, your brain has been beaten to a mush from all the studying, so when you say "it's your fault" it comes out as "it's <reading>yue</reading> fault!" Go ahead and say it out loud that way.

examples.en: When I was ferrying the prince across the river by boat to the opposite bank, an accident occurred.
examples.ja: 王子を船で川の向こう岸へ渡していた時に、事故が起きたんです。

examples.en: I had only owned the car for half a year, and I already got involved in an accident.
examples.ja: 車を買ってまだ半年しかたっていないのに、もう事故に巻きこまれてしまった。

examples.en: Due to the hit-and-run accident, the beef he just bought became ground beef.
examples.ja: ひき逃げ事故のせいで、買ったばかりの牛肉が挽き肉になった。

4934.meaning_mnemonic:
An <kanji>occurrence</kanji> that only results because of <kanji>circumstance</kanji>s is also called an <vocabulary>accident</vocabulary>. You didn't want this bad thing to happen, it was just an occurrence of circumstance! Everything aligned in the worst way.

事故 is mostly used to refer to physical accidents, like traffic accidents (交通事故) or construction accidents (建設事故). Sometimes other kinds of <vocabulary>mishap</vocabulary>s get the 事故 label too, like broadcast mishaps (放送事故), where something inappropriate or unplanned happens on air.
4934.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: I can't work because of my computer malfunction.
examples.ja: パソコンの故障で仕事ができない。

examples.en: That fax machine is out of order.
examples.ja: あのファックス機は故障中だよ。

examples.en: The WaniKani robot that Koichi spent a million dollars to create, malfunctioned within ten seconds of starting up.
examples.ja: コウイチが百万ドルをかけて制作したワニカニロボットは、起動してから十秒で故障してしまいました。

4935.meaning_mnemonic: By some <kanji>circumstance</kanji>, the thing you're using is <kanji>hinder</kanji>ing you. Usually it works, but now it's <vocabulary>out of order</vocabulary> and has a <vocabulary>malfunction</vocabulary>.
4935.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: I didn't intentionally mean to do it at all.
examples.ja: 故意にしたつもりは全くないんです。

examples.en: It was not on purpose, but it did cause you grief.
examples.ja: 故意ではありませんが、あなたを悲しませてしまったのは事実です。

examples.en: The disputed point here is whether it resulted from intentional or negligent conduct.
examples.ja: ここでは、故意または過失によるものだったかが争点となります。

examples.en: I plead guilty to intentionally eating Koichi’s secret bacon.
examples.ja: コウイチの秘密のベーコンを故意に食べた罪を認めます。

4936.meaning_mnemonic:
The <kanji>circumstance</kanji> was caused by the <kanji>idea</kanji> I had. Because I had this idea before the circumstance, it shows I was <vocabulary>intentional</vocabulary> in doing it. I did it <vocabulary>on purpose</vocabulary>.

Note that 故意 is mostly used in formal contexts.
4936.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: I am currently working at Panasonic Corporation.
examples.ja: 今はパナソニック株式会社で働いています。

examples.en: Tofugu is not a corporation; it's a limited liability company (LLC).
examples.ja: トーフグは株式会社じゃなくて合同会社ですよ。

examples.en: Can you call Sony Corporation to make sure the fax went through alright?
examples.ja: 株式会社ソニーに電話を入れて、ファックスの送信がきちんと完了しているかどうか確認してくれる？

4937.meaning_mnemonic: This <kanji>company</kanji> (会社) has done the <kanji>ritual</kanji> required to create <kanji>stock</kanji>s for their company. When a company has stocks, they become a <vocabulary>corporation</vocabulary>.
4937.reading_mnemonic: The readings for everything here are the readings you learned with the individual kanji, though not all are on'yomi. This word is usually rendaku'd too, but sometimes you'll see the non-rendaku version in romaji when it comes to English language legal stuff, so keep that in mind.

examples.en: My mother has very little knowledge about the stock market.
examples.ja: うちの母は、株式市場に関する知識はほとんどありません。

examples.en: The stock market is in the red today as many shares have dropped.
examples.ja: 多くの株が下落したため、今日の株式市場は真っ赤です。

examples.en: The global slowdown has significantly affected our stock market, as well.
examples.ja: 世界的な景気の減速は、私たちの株式市場にも影響を及ぼした。

examples.en: In Japan, there are seven stock markets: "First Section," "Second Section," "Mothers," "JASDAQ," "Prime Market," "Standard Market," and "Growth Market.”
examples.ja: 日本には、「市場第一部」、「市場第二部」、「マザーズ」、「JASDAQ」、「プライム市場」、「スタンダード市場」、「グロース市場」の七つの株式市場があります。

4938.meaning_mnemonic: The <kanji>location</kanji> in the <kanji>city</kanji> where the <kanji>stock</kanji>s <kanji>ritual</kanji> takes place is the <vocabulary>stock market</vocabulary>. Just think of what happens in a stock market... the stock ritual, where people buy and sell stocks. And, of course, this is located in the city.
4938.reading_mnemonic: The readings are all readings that you learned with the kanji, so as long as you remember them, you’re good to go!

examples.en: Don't compare me to other children. I am who I am.
examples.ja: 他の子と比較しないで。私は私なんだから。

examples.en: I have created comparative data on education between Japan and the United States.
examples.ja: 教育についての日米の比較データを作成しました。

examples.en: If you directly compare a false diamond with a real one, you’ll know which one is which right away.
examples.ja: 偽物のダイヤと本物のダイヤを直接比較してみれば、どっちがどっちだかすぐに分かるよ。

4939.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>compare</kanji> and <kanji>contrast</kanji> will give you a <vocabulary>comparison</vocabulary> of something.
4939.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: His forehead glistened with sweat.
examples.ja: 彼の額には、汗がキラキラ光っていた。

examples.en: I'm drenched in sweat. Could you please lower the temperature a bit more?
examples.ja: 汗だくなんだけど。もう少し温度下げてくれない？

examples.en: I'm a heavy sweater, so when I finally got to high-five my beloved idol, my hands were all sweaty and sticky.
examples.ja: 汗っかきなので、せっかく大好きなアイドルとハイタッチをするのに、汗で手がベタベタだったんです。

4940.meaning_mnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.
4940.reading_mnemonic: The reading is the same one you learned with the kanji. Also, your <vocabulary>sweat</vocabulary> smells like <reading>ass</reading> (あせ).

examples.en: Ugh, this shirt smells sweaty!
examples.ja: ゲッ、なんかこのシャツ、汗臭い！

examples.en: After three hours of exercise, it's no wonder I got sweaty and started to smell.
examples.ja: 三時間も運動したから、さすがに汗臭くなった。

examples.en: I liked his sweaty-smelling pillow.
examples.ja: 私は彼の汗臭い枕が好きだった。

4941.meaning_mnemonic: If your <kanji>sweat</kanji> is <kanji>smelly</kanji> (臭い) you are <vocabulary>sweaty-smelling</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>smelling of sweat</vocabulary>, or <vocabulary>smelling like sweat</vocabulary>.
4941.reading_mnemonic: The readings are the ones you learned with the kanji.

examples.en: I began to hear the sound of the river.
examples.ja: 河の音が聞こえてきました。

examples.en: Finally, a bridge has been built over that large river.
examples.ja: ついにあの大きな河に橋が掛かるそうだ。

examples.en: That river is very wide, so it would be impossible for horses to swim across.
examples.ja: あの河はとても広いので、馬が泳いで渡るのは無理でしょう。

4942.meaning_mnemonic:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. 

河 originally referred to the Yellow River in ancient China, so it's usually associated with very <vocabulary>large river</vocabulary>s. 河 is a lot less common than 川, but you might still find it in literature, where it can emphasize the grand and powerful nature of a river or its cultural significance.
4942.reading_mnemonic: The reading is the same like the word 川 which has the same meaning. Associate the two to remember!

examples.en: The suitcase that has a kappa sticker on it is my suitcase.
examples.ja: 河童のシールがはってあるスーツケースが私のスーツケースです。

examples.en: I saw a kappa eating cucumber sushi rolls.
examples.ja: 河童がかっぱ巻きを食べてるのを見たよ。

examples.en: Can you react as if you believe Kappa really exist?
examples.ja: まるで河童が存在していることを信じているかのようにリアクションしてもらえますか？

examples.en: That kappa has really limited views.
examples.ja: あの河童は本当に視野が狭い。

4943.meaning_mnemonic: A <kanji>river</kanji> <kanji>juvenile</kanji>... not what you think. It's a <vocabulary>kappa</vocabulary>, a mythological Japanese creature. That being said, it lives in / around rivers and is about the size of a juvenile, so maybe this makes sense.
4943.reading_mnemonic: The reading for 河 makes sense. The reading for 童 however is weird. Since the meaning is "kappa" though you can use that to remember the reading as well. If you don't know what a kappa is do some research on the internets and figure out about them. It's interesting, and it will help you to remember this word.

examples.en: This is a fossil of a mammoth that lived during the glacial epoch.
examples.ja: これは、氷河期に生きていたマンモスの化石です。

examples.en: Viet is planning to go to Athabasca Glacier for his next vacation to take glacier photos.
examples.ja: ビエトは、氷河の写真をとるために、次のバケーションでアサバスカ氷河へ行く予定です。

examples.en: I saw a glistening blue glacier in the distance.
examples.ja: 遠くのほうにキラキラと青く光る氷河が見えました。

examples.en: The number of melting glaciers has been increasing every year due to global warming.
examples.ja: 地球温暖化のために、毎年溶けている氷河が増えている。

4944.meaning_mnemonic: An <kanji>ice</kanji> <kanji>river</kanji> is some ice that moves (very slowly) like a river. That is a <vocabulary>glacier</vocabulary>. In fact, many inlets and sounds were created with glaciers, because glaciers moved through them like rivers... not very quickly, though.
4944.reading_mnemonic: The reading for 氷 is the one you didn't learn. Think of the glacier coming slowly to your door. It rings your doorbell and says <reading>heyo</reading> (ひょう). Note that the か becomes が here.

examples.en: I'd love to see the Panama Canal.
examples.ja: パナマ運河を見てみたいです。

examples.en: You can skate on the canal during the winter.
examples.ja: 冬には運河の上でスケートができますよ。

examples.en: If this canal didn't exist, I don't think this country would have developed this far.
examples.ja: この運河がなかったら、この国はここまで発展しなかったでしょう。

4945.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well. The か goes to が, probably while floating down said <vocabulary>canal</vocabulary>.

examples.en: "I’ll have a blowfish and tofu sandwich." "I’ll have the same."
examples.ja: 「豆腐と河豚のサンドイッチをお願いします。」 「同じく。」

examples.en: I happened to witness that Fugu slipped some money into Salmon's hand.
examples.ja: 河豚がサーモンの手にそっとお金を渡したのを見ちゃったんだよ。

examples.en: The pufferfish that I'm gonna go eat tonight has been occupying my mind and I can't get any work done.
examples.ja: 夜に食べに行く河豚のことが心を占めていて、仕事が手につきません。

4946.meaning_mnemonic:
The <kanji>river</kanji> <kanji>pig</kanji> is what's known as <vocabulary>fugu</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>blowfish</vocabulary>. You may know it from our mascot and best friend, the Tofugu!

But why does "river pig" = fugu? It's true that fugu usually live in the ocean, but sometimes they make their way into rivers near the ocean too. The "pig" part probably comes from their round, puffed-up appearance.
4946.reading_mnemonic: The reading makes no sense, really. Neither kanji readings work. But, if you remember that a river pig is a fugu, you can know the reading is <reading>ふぐ</reading>as well! YOU ARE A BLOWFISH, JESSE!

examples.en: Koichi's dancing is always intense.
examples.ja: コウイチのダンスはいつも激しいです。

examples.en: The sound of fierce rain and wind was heard from outside.
examples.ja: 外からは激しい雨風の音が聞こえてきていた。

examples.en: My father and mother often have heated arguments.
examples.ja: うちの父と母は、よく激しい口論をする。

examples.en: Sometimes at night I feel an intense anxiety.
examples.ja: 時々、夜になると激しい不安を感じるの。

4947.meaning_mnemonic: This is a single kanji with an い on the end, meaning you know it's probably an adjective. What's the adjective form of <kanji>fierce</kanji> and <kanji>violent</kanji>? <vocabulary>Fierce</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>violent</vocabulary>! That's <vocabulary>intense</vocabulary>.
4947.reading_mnemonic: What is <vocabulary>fierce</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>violent</vocabulary>? That old <reading>hag</reading> (はげ). Imagine her coming at you attacking you violently!

examples.en: Is this burnable trash? Is it non-burnable trash?
examples.ja: これは燃えるゴミですか？燃えないゴミですか？

examples.en: This is easy to burn, so please don't use it near fire.
examples.ja: これは燃えやすいから火のそばで使わないでください。

examples.en: I'm feeling really fired up for the first time in a long while!
examples.ja: なんか久々に燃えてきた！

examples.en: This tweet is definitely going to cause a major controversy.
examples.ja: このツイート、ゼッタイめっちゃ燃えるよ。

4948.meaning_mnemonic:
Remember how 燃やす means "to burn something" or "to set on fire”? Well, 燃える is the version that means <vocabulary>to burn</vocabulary> or <vocabulary>to be on fire</vocabulary>. You might say that paper and wood 燃える easily, for example. And if your house is 燃えている, you're in trouble.

You can remember this slightly different meaning for 燃える because of the える part, which refers to the letter "L." And the "L" stands for "love" — as in your passionate, burning love for kanji.
4948.reading_mnemonic: The reading is the same as the word 燃やす.

examples.en: The fire that started from the cigarette has finally gone out.
examples.ja: タバコから燃え付いた火がやっと消えました。

examples.en: It didn't take long for the fire to spread to other things from there.
examples.ja: そこから他のものに火が燃え付くのに時間はかからなかった。

examples.en: While conducting a chemistry experiment, my bangs caught fire.
examples.ja: 化学の実験をしている最中に、前髪に火が燃え付いた。

4949.meaning_mnemonic: When something <kanji>attach</kanji>es a <kanji>burn</kanji> to something that something is about <vocabulary>to catch fire</vocabulary>.
4949.reading_mnemonic: This is the readings of 燃える and 付く put together.

examples.en: After losing everything, I ended up all alone.
examples.ja: 全てを失って、独りぼっちになってしまった。

examples.en: It seems like I have to live alone from now on.
examples.ja: これからずっと独りで生きなくちゃいけないのか。

examples.en: He lives alone too.
examples.ja: 彼も独りで住んでいるよ。

4950.meaning_mnemonic:
The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well.

While 一人 simply means "one person," 独り carries a stronger sense of being <vocabulary>alone</vocabulary>, often with connotations of <vocabulary>solitude</vocabulary>. It can also mean someone is <vocabulary>single</vocabulary> (as in not married).
4950.reading_mnemonic: The reading is different from the one you learned (this is kun'yomi). There's an easy way to remember it, though. 一人 and 独り share the same readings and mean almost the same thing. Just try to remember that this ひとり is used to emphasize solitude.

examples.en: This is privilege for the unmarried, isn't this?
examples.ja: これって独身の特権だよね。

examples.en: He got a taste of success through lying about being unmarried.
examples.ja: アイツ、独身ってウソを付くことに味を占めちゃったんだよ。

examples.en: I used to ride a motorcycle when I was single, but it's dangerous. So now, thinking about my family, I don’t ride anymore.
examples.ja: 独身時代はバイクに乗ってましたが、危険なので家族のことを考えて今はもう乗っていません。

examples.en: I’m single and looking for someone I can marry. That’s really it for now. But please do not hesitate to contact me if you need any further information about me.
examples.ja: 私は独身で、婚活中です。とりあえずそんな感じですが、何か他に聞きたいことがあれば、遠慮なくご連絡ください。

4951.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Sakura-chan, your cat has unique eyes, don't you think?
examples.ja: 桜ちゃんの猫は、目が独特だよね。

examples.en: That comedian's unique way of speaking adds a lot of flavor.
examples.ja: あのコメディアンは、独特な口調がいい味を出している。

examples.en: These spices have a unique aroma.
examples.ja: この香辛料は独特の香りがする。

4952.meaning_mnemonic: It is <kanji>alone</kanji> and <kanji>special</kanji>. Nothing is like it. It is very <vocabulary>unique</vocabulary> and <vocabulary>peculiar</vocabulary>.
4952.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: July 4th is the Independence Day of the United States.
examples.ja: 七月四日はアメリカ独立記念日です。

examples.en: I'm working hard to pursue independent entrepreneurship.
examples.ja: 私は独立開業を目指して頑張っています。

examples.en: That company has an independent relationship with our company.
examples.ja: あの会社は、うちの会社とは独立した関係にあります。

examples.en: If you say not many people who left the company and went independent succeeded, show me the data, their plans, and how they failed.
examples.ja: 会社を辞めて独立した人で成功した人は多くないって言うなら、そのデータやその人たちの計画、そしてどうしてそれが失敗したのかを示してくださいよ。

4953.meaning_mnemonic:
<kanji>Alone</kanji> I <kanji>stand</kanji>. I have at last gained my <vocabulary>independence</vocabulary>!

独立 implies breaking off or separating from something or someone and achieving independent <vocabulary>autonomy</vocabulary>. While it can also refer to self-reliance, it's more commonly associated with political independence or independence from organizations.
4953.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: Oh, did you study all of it through self-studying!?
examples.ja: え、全部、独学で勉強したんですか！？

examples.en: You can look up any number of self-study methods on the Internet.
examples.ja: 独学の方法なんて、インターネットがあればいくらでも調べられるじゃない。

examples.en: Isn't self-studying inefficient?
examples.ja: 独学で学ぶのは効率が悪いんじゃない？

examples.en: Due to the spread of the Internet, it’s become much easier to learn other languages through self-study nowadays.
examples.ja: インターネットの普及によって、独学で外国語を勉強することは昔よりもずっと簡単になった。

4954.meaning_mnemonic: You are <kanji>alone</kanji> in your <kanji>study</kanji>. You are studying on your own. This is <vocabulary>self study</vocabulary>.
4954.reading_mnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. If you know the readings of your kanji you'll know how to read this as well.

examples.en: The beast was caught in the trap!
examples.ja: 獣がワナにかかったぞ！

examples.en: A large beast lives in the forest.
examples.ja: 森に大きな獣が一匹住んでいる。

examples.en: That guy has eyes like a beast. I’m scared.
examples.ja: あの男の人、獣のような目をしていて、恐いわ。

4955.reading_mnemonic:

4960.meaning_mnemonic:
Because the hiragana ends with an う sound, you know this word is a verb. The kanji itself means <kanji>stab</kanji> so the verb vocab version must also be <vocabulary>to stab</vocabulary>.

Wondering how it's different from 刺す? 突く refers to the act of pushing or pressing something with a tip of an object, often done forcefully and swiftly. So when you use 突く as in "to stab," your focus is on the forcefulness of the action. On the other hand, 刺す focuses more on the actual act of piercing into something or someone with a sharp thing. 

This is why 突く can be be translated many ways, like <vocabulary>to poke</vocabulary>, <vocabulary>to jab</vocabulary>, and many more.

4966.meaning_mnemonic:
触る means "to touch," and 触れる also means <vocabulary>to touch</vocabulary>. The word also means <vocabulary>to touch on</vocabulary>, as in touching on some subject. Just think of a subject that is <reading>rare</reading> (れる) for you to want to touch on.

触れる is often for when something happens <vocabulary>to come into contact with</vocabulary> something, possibly in a fleeting or momentary way. It's still used in phrases like "When I touched your hand," but has a lighter, more indirect and literary feel than 触る, which conveys a greater sense of purpose and intent behind the action.

触れる is often used in constructions like 手がカバンに触れる (one's hand touches a bag), where が indicates what's doing the touching and に marks what's being touched. If you see を instead of が, 触れる becomes transitive, changing the meaning to "to have your hand touch a bag."
